transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. To get us started, could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Um, well, I came in because I just feel worn out all the time. It's like, even if I get a full night's sleep and stay in bed, I wake up and my body just feels heavy... like it's made of sandbags or something. Just getting through a normal workday, or even doing something simple like folding the laundry, it just takes absolutely everything I have. I don't know why I'm so exhausted, but it's really starting to affect me.
Do you find that you have lost interest or pleasure in the activities that you used to enjoy?

Yeah, I really have. Um, I used to always make time for things I liked doing... like hiking, yoga, working in my garden. I also used to love going out and taking bird photos. But lately, I just keep canceling on people, or I just let my camera sit in the closet. Honestly, none of it even feels worth the effort right now.
Have you noticed any changes in your sensitivity to cold, such as feeling cold when others around you are comfortable?
No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I think I feel pretty normal when it comes to the temperature... just the same as anyone else around me, really.
Have you ever experienced a period of feeling this way in the past, perhaps months or years ago?

No, I don't think so. Um, I mean, I've had stressful weeks at work where I was tired, but... nothing like this. I can't really remember a time in the past where I felt this completely drained and just uninterested in everything. It feels pretty new to me.
Have you been told, or do you have any reason to believe, that you snore loudly or stop breathing while you are sleeping?
No, nobody's ever mentioned anything like that to me. I don't think I snore loudly, and I've never woken up gasping for air or anything. As far as I know, my breathing is fine when I sleep.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or your weight since you started feeling this way?
No, not really. My appetite has been about the same as usual. I haven't noticed any weight gain or loss, either. Everything on that front seems pretty normal.
Have you noticed if other people have mentioned that you seem to be moving or speaking much more slowly than usual?

Actually, yes. My husband has pointed that out. He says I move around the house like I'm underwater lately. And, um, if he asks me something really simple, it can take me a while to answer him. He told me the words just come out so slowly right now.
Looking back over your entire life, can you recall any other time, even if it was years ago, where you felt this same way for at least two weeks?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had times where I felt down or stressed out for a few days, but... no, I can't recall a time where I felt exactly like this for two whole weeks. This is really the first time it's been this heavy for this long, as far as I can remember.
Have you had any thoughts that life is not worth living or that you would be better off dead?

Yes, I have. Mostly late at night, when it's quiet. I catch myself thinking that my husband might just be better off without me. I haven't made any kind of plan to do anything, but... the thought keeps coming back, and it honestly scares me.
Are you still able to carry out your basic daily responsibilities, such as working or taking care of your personal hygiene, even if it takes a significant amount of effort?

I'm doing the basics, but it takes everything I have. Um, most of my energy right now just goes into getting through work and doing the bare minimum at home. I've actually fallen behind on my client reports... and I've started avoiding my friends. I even stopped the outdoor routines that usually keep me steady. So, yes, I'm keeping up with my hygiene and going to my job, but that's really all I can manage right now.
